sections.title: The End Times and Resurrection
observations: Daniel 12 begins with a focus on the end times, emphasizing a time of great distress unlike any that has occurred before. This sets the stage for the ultimate resolution of God's plan for His people.

The mention of Michael, the great prince, signifies God's protection over His people during this tumultuous period. Michael's role as a protector is a comforting reminder of God's sovereignty and care for His faithful.

The resurrection of the dead is a pivotal theme in this chapter, indicating that all will be raised—some to everlasting life and others to shame and everlasting contempt. This dual resurrection underscores the finality of God's judgment.

sections.title: The Sealing of the Book
observations: Daniel is instructed to seal the book until the time of the end, suggesting that some prophecies will remain hidden until the appropriate time. This highlights the mystery of God's plan and the importance of patience and faithfulness in waiting for its fulfillment.

The inquiry about the duration of these events reflects a common human desire to understand God's timeline. However, the response emphasizes that knowledge will increase in the last days, indicating a divine revelation of truth as history unfolds.

sections.title: The Call to Endurance
observations: The chapter concludes with a call for endurance and faithfulness. The promise of reward for those who remain steadfast in their faith is a central theme, encouraging believers to persevere through trials and tribulations.

The mention of the specific time periods (1,290 days and 1,335 days) serves to remind readers that God's timing is different from human understanding, and that faithfulness is required regardless of the circumstances.

importantVerses.commentary: At that time Michael, the great prince who protects your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress such as has not happened from the beginning of nations until then. But at that time your people—everyone whose name is found written in the book—will be delivered.
Multitudes who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake: some to everlasting life, others to shame and everlasting contempt.
But you, Daniel, close up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.

questions: What does the role of Michael as a protector reveal about God's care for His people during times of distress?
How should believers interpret the sealing of the book in relation to understanding prophecy?
What implications does the resurrection of the dead have for our understanding of eternal life and judgment?
How can we apply the call to endurance in our own lives, especially in the face of trials?
